input: n is an integer with 0 <= n <= 30. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. return: The exact number of structurally distinct binary search trees containing n distinct ordered keys. n = 0 returns 1 for the empty tree. Key labels and actual tree objects are not input or output.
mutation_aliasing: No mutable input exists. A private count array is allocated; only an integer scalar is returned. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Every Catalan count C_i for i <= 30 is at most C_30 = 3814986502092304, below 9007199254740991. Each product C_left*C_right is a nonnegative summand of C_size, and each accumulating prefix sum is at most C_size, so every multiplication and addition stays exact in both languages. Larger n is outside the paired domain, even though Python could retain larger integers.
complexity: O(n*n + 1) time and O(n + 1) auxiliary space. For each size, enumerate every split into left_size and size-left_size-1, multiplying already computed independent subtree counts. There is no recursive tree enumeration or hidden output allocation.
